validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki. Two Uzbek news outlets, three months apart, name the segment explicitly and with real engineering specificity that is not plausibly fabricated: uzreport.news (2020-09-09, live-verified) reports 'Зирабулакское УМГ, капремонт МГ «Мубарек-Зирабулак» (БГР-ТБА) I, II, III нитки, участок 50-78 км (Ø1020х12 мм - 2,1 км)' and, in a second project entry on the same page, 'Капремонт МГ «Мубарек-Зирабулак» I, II нитки, участок 3-50 км (Ø1020х12 мм - 8,0 км)'; kun.uz (2020-12-26, live-verified) separately names 'Мубарек - Зирабулак' among the lines Epsilon EDC was modernizing, in an article about raising corridor throughput from 67 to 72 million m3/day. The sheet's existing Facebook ref (Epsilon EDC, Nov 2020, URL slug decodes to 'preparation under way to commission the first string of the Mubarek-Zirabulak pipeline') is consistent with the same project and returns 200. CAVEAT: all three of these ultimately trace to Epsilon EDC's own PR material picked up by different outlets on different dates, not to fully separate origins, so I am NOT calling this the 2-independent-origin 'high' bar -- tier medium on existence, though the level of technical detail (named nitki, exact diameter+wall thickness, exact km-post windows) makes fabrication implausible. I could not find a second, genuinely separate-origin source (checked Мубарекнефтегазмонтаж/mngmaj.uz -- expired TLS cert, unreachable; checked bgps.uz's completed-works list -- reachable, mentions Мубарек infrastructure (a gas processing plant and a compressor station) but never 'Зирабулак' or this pipeline, so NOT used as corroboration despite a search-engine summary claiming otherwise -- that summary could not be substantiated against the live page text and is flagged here as a near-miss, not cited).
CLASSIFICATION: Gas transmission trunk line is correct -- it is explicitly a 'магистральный газопровод' (МГ) segment of the БГР-ТБА (Bukhara Gas Region-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty) system per both sources, consistent with GEM's own OtherLanguageSegmentName='БГР-ТБА' and OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName='Газопровод "Мубарек-Зирабулак", 1-ая нитка' (both already on the sheet and consistent with the sources' 'I нитка' naming).
DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any roster row. P6934/P6935 (same PipelineName, 'II'/'III' presumed segment names) are NOT the same pipe as P6933 -- uzreport.news affirmatively describes I, II and III as three separate physical strings ('нитки') all under simultaneous capital repair, the Kazakhstan cluster-A pattern (parallel strings = real, separate pipe unless a source says otherwise) applies directly and is NOT refuted here. P6936 (Kelif-Mubarek) and P6965/P6966 (Mubarek-Kagan) are different corridors (Kelif->Mubarek and Mubarek->Kagan respectively, vs this row's Mubarek->Zirabulak) -- no overlap.
ATTRIBUTION: StartLocation=Mubarek / EndLocation=Zirabulak, both Uzbekistan -- consistent across both sources, no geocoder red flags, both are known Uzbek gas-infrastructure toponyms along the BGR-TBA corridor (Zirabulak sits on the Bukhara-Samarkand corridor the line follows toward the Kyrgyz/Kazakh export leg). Owner/Operator = Uztransgaz -- see fills below for refs; the value itself is correct and unchanged, this is a ref-sourcing question only.
SPEC: Diameter=1020mm CONFIRMED directly against uzreport.news ('Ø1020х12 мм' cited for the I/II/III нитки repair sections) -- the sheet's existing Diameter ref (same URL) was flagged in existing_ref_checks as a ReadTimeout; re-verified live now (url_verifier: OK, 200, contains 'Мубарек' and '1020') -- that was a transient timeout, not a dead link, no change needed. Length: LengthKnownKm is blank and LengthEstimateKm=131.17 is geometry-derived (very-low-accuracy mapped route), not a sourced value -- I looked hard at whether uzreport.news's km-window figures ('участок 3-50 км', 'участок 50-78 км', repair lengths 8.0km and 2.1km) could ground a Length fill and concluded they cannot: re-fetched the full sentence context and both figures describe the LENGTH OF PIPE REPLACED within a repair project inside a stated km-post window along the corridor, not the segment's own end-to-end length -- staging either figure as Length would be a fabrication dressed as a citation, so left alone (UNRESOLVED, correctly). Capacity/StartYearEarliest: blank on the sheet, no source found naming a capacity or construction year for this specific string (as opposed to the aggregate BTBA corridor figure) -- left blank rather than forcing a number, per instructions.
STATUS: see status_reviews.

fills.researcher_notes: Operator field was MISSING_REF. Cited a primary legal source (Uzbekistan government decree No. 585 of 23.12.1992, 'On the creation of the Uzbek state association for natural gas transportation "Uztransgaz"', lex.uz) establishing Uztransgaz as the state-created single operator of enterprises performing pipeline gas transport, operation and repair of magistral (trunk) gas pipelines throughout Uzbekistan -- which by its own text covers this Mubarek-Zirabulak trunk line, since it is explicitly a магистральный газопровод (МГ). Corroborated by an independent 2019 Gazeta.uz news article on Uztransgaz's corporate restructuring (separation from Uzbekneftegaz), confirming it as a real, currently-existing, independently-reported entity in the same role. Both URLs verified live via url_verifier. Did not attempt to source a segment-specific 'Uztransgaz operates THIS line' statement -- none needed given the decree's blanket, still-current jurisdiction over all Uzbek trunk gas pipelines; the value itself (Узтрансгаз) is unchanged from what NF's OtherLanguage fields already implied.

The existing Owner ref (https://utg.uz/ru/about/history/) is a CONFIRMED genuine HTTP 404 (re-verified today, not a transient block/timeout -- this matches the country note's already-known finding on this exact URL). Per the hard access-failure rule, a confirmed 404 is one of the two cases that may legitimately drop a ref, so I am not keeping the dead live URL as-is; per the archiving convention I am NOT deleting the citation either, I am replacing it with its live Wayback capture (20260314231446, re-verified today: OK/200, contains 'Узтрансгаз' -- the earlier note that web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable all of 2026-08-26 did not reproduce for me this run) plus the same lex.uz decree used for Operator above, as a second independent corroborating source for '100% Uztransgaz' ownership of Uzbekistan's trunk gas network. Owner value itself is unchanged.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Both sources describe active CAPITAL REPAIR (капремонт) and modernization of an already-existing, in-service line -- by definition a line being overhauled to raise throughput (67->72 mcm/day per kun.uz) is an operating asset, not a proposed/under-construction one; the sheet's Status [ref] substring check flagged 'operating' as literally absent, which is the known prose-equivalence false negative (no Russian-language article uses the English word) -- content substantively supports the status. Newest evidence specifically naming this segment is 2020-12 (kun.uz). Searched for 2023-2026 segment-specific news and found none, but did find general, live-verified evidence that Uztransgaz's trunk network remains actively operated and invested in: a July-2024 Uztransgaz corporate-news item on inspection/repair work at compressor station KS-2 under the Zirabulak directorate (УМГ Зирабулак) -- URL located via search but I could NOT independently re-verify its body text against a direct fetch (the site renders via client-side JS/Bitrix and static fetches return only the page shell), so it is NOT cited as a proposed_ref here, only noted; and a live-verified Uztransgaz news page on the Gazli directorate's autumn-winter-2024/2025 seasonal preparations. No indication anywhere of shelving, cancellation, or decommissioning. Dormancy rules do not apply (status is operating, not proposed/shelved). Verdict: confirm, at the segment-specific 2020-12 evidence date, with network-level context supporting continuity through 2024-2025.
